title: The popular version. Marie Curie's notebooks are still radioactive.
description:
Marie Curie's notebooks are still radioactive. That part is true. They sit in lead-lined boxes at France's national library in Paris.

Visitors sign a liability waiver first. They also wear protective gear to open the boxes.

The half-life of radium-226, the most common radium isotope. Her papers are still radioactive after more than a century.

She carried radium and polonium in her coat pocket. She also kept them in a desk drawer. The source does not say how the contamination reached each page, so this reel does not guess.

Her clothes, furniture and cookbooks are listed as well. ScienceAlert reports that her laboratory notes are still radioactive too.

Her research is still giving off its own evidence.

Sources:
- https://www.csmonitor.com/Innovation/Horizons/2011/1107/Marie-Curie-Why-her-papers-are-still-radioactive (read): Curie's manuscripts are kept in lead-lined boxes in the Pierre and Marie Curie collection at France's national library; visitors must wear protective clothing and sign a waiver of liability; radium-226, the most common radium isotope, has a half-life of 1,601 years; she carried polonium and radium in her coat pocket and kept them in a desk drawer; her papers are still radioactive after more than 100 years.
- https://www.sciencealert.com/these-personal-effects-of-marie-curie-will-be-radioactive-for-another-1-500-years (read): much of her personal effects including clothes, furniture, cookbooks and laboratory notes are still radioactive; her laboratory notebooks are stored in lead-lined boxes at the Bibliotheque Nationale in Paris; visitors are expected to sign a liability waiver and wear protective gear; radium-226 half-life given as about 1,600 years.
